Date: 2026-08-04T20:10:00Z
Subject: RE: RetailNova — sudden throughput collapse during peak (noon PST)

Quick findings from the initial triage (ops ran trace for 11:45–12:10 PST window):
- No deployment on our side during the window. Control-plane change logs show a transient BGP flap on one of the peering appliances at 11:52:07 PST that resulted in asymmetric path selection for some RetailNova prefixes.
- DNS: RetailNova's zone returned an old A record for proxy-ingress that pointed to the legacy peering NAT IP for a subset of egress nodes (~12% of queries). That caused ~1/8 of flows to be routed through the legacy NAT/proxy chain which has a long queue depth under load.
- Proxy metrics: proxy-queue-length and proxy-backpressure spiked on the legacy path; we see long queue waits and connection resets which surfaced as 502/504 at the application layer. Attached are route-dump-20260804.txt and proxy-queue-stats-08-04.csv.

Temporary mitigations applied at 20:02Z:
1) Forced failover: we withdrew the legacy peering advertisement and routed affected prefixes to the primary dedicated peer for RetailNova (expected cutover within a minute).
2) Lifted proxy keepalive settings on the legacy appliances to reduce head-of-line blocking.
3) Applied a short-lived rate-limit on background batch inference for RetailNova to reduce pressure while failover converges.

Observed status after mitigations:
- Error rates dropped to baseline after ~90s of convergence. Throughput recovered gradually, tail latency back to ~120ms.

Next steps I recommend:
- Full packet-level correlation to confirm no request-level corruption.
- Permanent DNS sweep to remove stale A records on RetailNova side (looks like a zone publish artifact).
- We should add automated cross-checks between peering route table state and DNS records to detect this class of mismatch.

I'll prepare a short incident timeline for the postmortem.

— Vivek

Subject: RetailNova incident summary and next steps (post-incident)

Sara / Tom — thank you for your patience and for the quick logs. Below is a short summary and the action items we will deliver in the postmortem. Please let us know if you prefer a follow-up call with our engineering leadership.

Incident summary (high level):
- Impact: 11:52–11:55 PST — partial routing to legacy peering path caused proxy queueing; effective throughput reduced and 5xx error spike reported by RetailNova. Peak error rate ~14% for affected flows.
- Root cause (preliminary): DNS and peering state mismatch; a stale A record in RetailNova's DNS returned the legacy NAT/proxy address for a subset of requests which were then routed over a path with inadequate queue headroom under load. BGP flap amplified the distribution of requests across both paths.
- Mitigation performed: forced withdrawal of legacy advertisement, re-route to dedicated peer, reduced proxy keepalive to reduce head-of-line blocking, short throttle on non-critical batch inference. Error rates returned to baseline after ~90s post-failover.

Deliverables and timeline:
1) Incident timeline and packet-level correlation: 48 hours (Vivek / infra) — will include exact counts and sample traces.
2) DNS sweep verification: 24 hours (RetailNova + Redwood recommended playbook) — we will share a small script to detect stale A records and coordinate with your DNS admin.
3) Automated guardrails: 2 weeks — create a cross-check that validates peering route advertisements against published DNS records for customer-critical prefixes; will propose implementation and rollout plan.
4) Post-incident review (internal): schedule within 72 hours, invite RetailNova for a technical review.

Temporary goodwill: Marissa will follow up re: any service credit you may request after we finalize the postmortem.

Please reply if you'd like a synchronous review — we're available this afternoon PST for a technical triage call.

Thanks again,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
